correctness.rationale: TARGET-route proof verified step by step: cof(R)=R on SO(3) and cof(alpha Q)=alpha^2 Q=alpha F hold; cof entries are quadratic quasiaffine hence Jensen equality is admissible at p=2 for compactly supported homogeneous gradient Young measures; M1+M2=t0 I and M1+alpha M2=t0^2 I solve to M1=M2=(t0/2)I=(9/16)I; tr(R)<=3 gives lambda>=9/16 and 1-lambda>=9/20 summing to 81/80>1, contradiction including edge cases lambda in {0,1}. Exact Fractions artifacts reproduce all numbers. The supplementary rank remark overstates intra-well ranks as {0,2,3} instead of {0,2}, immaterial to S3.

originality.rationale: The exact headline (alpha=1.25, barycenter 9/8 I, no homogeneous W^{1,2} gradient Young measure on SO(3) U 1.25 SO(3)) is substantively implied by stronger published results, so it is a corollary/recomputation rather than a new claim. Ball-James 2015 proves general incompatibility of dilatational wells k1 SO(3), k2 SO(3) for compact disjoint k1,k2 with p-transfer via Lemma 1, instantiated at {1},{1.25}; Zhang 1997 Thm 1.1 (n>=2, body-verified) gives QCH(SO(3))=SO(3), which by dilation-invariance excludes 9/8 I from each single well. Their conjunction implies the headline. D-K-M-S 2000 scope, delimited via body-inspected Ball-James account, is restricted sufficient conditions and does not itself cover this dilatational pair.

value.rationale: Although the TARGET S3 question is proved in vacuous form by a correct short argument at a motivated symmetric midpoint, the exact datum is mechanically implied by the stronger recorded dilatational-incompatibility plus single-well-hull theorems, so it fails the 'not known or mechanically implied' condition for a narrow exact invariant.
